title: Cognitive Dissonance as a Model for Conflicting Fine-Tuning Signals

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting cross-domain hypothesis: if LLMs resolve value conflicts predictably via cognitive-dissonance-like patterns, this provides a theory for auditing behavior under norm conflict. The chain is plausible but speculative — the analogy may not hold.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing conflicting-norm fine-tuning data is conceptually accessible. Fine-tuning a small model is feasible. Probing for behavioral inconsistency patterns requires careful experimental design. Mapping results to Festinger's theory is interpretive work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Open-ended: constructing conflicting norms, fine-tuning, probing for inconsistency, then interpreting through a cognitive science lens. The interpretive component (mapping to Festinger) has no clear stopping criterion. High risk of scope expansion.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
